clue.text: Tick off a debit?

parts.note: tick is slang for buying on account, and 'off' reads as its absence: a debit is the opposite of money owed to you on the books

explanation.surface: An accountant marks a debit entry as checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick off' looks like marking a list item; here 'tick' is British slang for buying on account, and 'off' means not available.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit entry is the reverse of an amount owed to you, and a shop refusing tick refuses this.

clue.text: A growing source of irritation

parts.note: growing reads literally as a plant in the ground, one that stings the skin

explanation.surface: Something becoming more and more annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' suggests increasing; it means a living plant whose leaves sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging weed whose hairs cause a skin rash is a plant that irritates.

clue.text: A, pound in cash for a low, wheeled carriage

indicators.note: the A and pound are placed inside the word cash

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Paying a pound in cash for an old low carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn vehicle with low wheels and a folding hood was this carriage.

clue.text: I leant out to settle on a series of heirs

definitions.text: settle on a series of heirs

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaning out to bequeath property down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I LEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to restrict an estate's inheritance to a fixed line of successors is this verb.

clue.text: Something one isn't allowed to do

definitions.text: Something one isn't allowed to do

parts.words: Something one isn't allowed to do
parts.note: a plain description of a deed forbidden under the law

explanation.surface: A rule naming forbidden behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed forbidden by law, a crime, is something prohibited.

clue.text: Clamour raised by lots of people

definitions.text: Clamour raised by lots of people

parts.words: Clamour raised by lots of people
parts.note: a plain description of the noisy confused din of a crowd all talking at once

explanation.surface: A crowd lifts its voices in a great noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar or din of many voices is a commotion of exactly this kind.

clue.text: Lady was meditative, as allegedly Queen Victoria was

parts.note: Una is a lady's name, the heroine of Spenser's Faerie Queene
mused means was thoughtful

explanation.surface: A lady lost in thought, like the old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is reputed to have said 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria's famous remark said she was not entertained, the state described.

clue.text: Old Nick in Paris?

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison, so an old prison in the French capital

explanation.surface: The Devil paying a visit to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' looks like the Devil; 'nick' is British slang for a jail, and this was the old fortress prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress prison in Paris stormed at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Exclusively youthful section of the aristocracy?

definitions.text: Exclusively youthful section of the aristocracy?

parts.words: Exclusively youthful section of the aristocracy
parts.note: a group kept young only by banning older members would have a ban on years, and this rank of nobles reads that way

explanation.surface: A clique of young nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BAR ON AGE: a group that excludes the old.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of lords of the rank below viscount is the whole class of that peerage.

clue.text: Revealing story of Swiss resistance?

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary hero of Swiss resistance to Austrian rule
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A story revealing secrets about the Swiss resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story of Swiss resistance' is the tale of Tell, so the pieces come out in the order Tell, tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway sign that discloses something hidden is called this, used as an adjective.

clue.text: A small cable was crumpled in her grasp

indicators.note: something held in her grasp sits inside the word her
something held in her grasp sits inside the word her

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: crumpled means the letters of 'was' are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman crushes a length of cable in her fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' and 'in her grasp' are both indicators; the surface reads them as a woman crushing something in her hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick rope or wire used for mooring or towing a ship is a nautical cable of this kind.

clue.text: Plenty of sadistic corporal punishment

definitions.meaning: a large quantity, as in 'cake with plenty of cream'

explanation.surface: A great deal of cruel physical punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a generous amount, and also whippings given with a lash.

clue.text: Trouble afoot with a second-class match?

parts.note: B is a grade below A, second class
a union is a match, as in marriage

explanation.surface: A second-rate marriage brings trouble on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble afoot' suggests impending difficulty; read it literally as a problem on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling at the base of the big toe is a foot complaint.

clue.text: The last thing one should do when felling a tree!

definitions.text: The last thing one should do when felling a tree!

parts.words: The last thing one should do when felling a tree
parts.note: the final step for a woodcutter is to move out of the way as the trunk falls

explanation.surface: Advice for a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing one should do' sounds like something forbidden; it is the final step.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving away from danger as the trunk comes down is the woodman's final safety step.

clue.text: See that the standard is kept up

definitions.text: See that the standard is kept up

parts.words: See that the standard is kept up
parts.note: the standard reads as a banner on a pole rather than a level of quality, kept up by being hoisted

explanation.surface: An instruction to maintain high standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality; it is a flag, and keeping it up means flying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To display a banner aloft, and so show loyalty or patriotism, is this idiom.

clue.text: Perpetrator of 4 about to close a bid?

indicators.note: about means the bid goes round the word for closing

parts.note: an offer is a bid
to end is to close

explanation.surface: A criminal is about to close a bid at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 refers to the clue at 4 down, whose answer is a deed against the law; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits a crime is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Woodland flowers one names incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone gets the names of wild flowers wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges ONE NAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood windflowers bloom on forest floors in spring.

clue.text: Rousing game on the coast of Holland?

definitions.meaning: driving birds such as pheasants up from cover for the guns
a port in the Netherlands, known in Dutch as Vlissingen

explanation.surface: Beaters starting birds on the Dutch shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Game here is wild birds hunted for sport; the second sense is the English name of the Dutch port Vlissingen.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling birds from cover in shooting is one sense; a port on the Dutch Scheldt estuary is the other.

clue.text: Close of play?

parts.note: close of play is the cricket phrase for the end of a day's play, read here as the end of a stage drama

explanation.surface: Stumps are drawn at the end of a day's cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close of play' is the cricket term for the day's end; here the play is a theatre piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The last episode on stage before the curtain falls ends a drama.

clue.text: Take exception to an article, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a thing or item; also, in grammar, the noun a verb acts on

explanation.surface: Disputing the use of a word in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is one sense; a thing or item is the other.

clue.text: The funds Simeon converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Simeon changed the money into another currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges SIMEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums of cash, plural, are money held.

clue.text: Foolish person holding fixed property

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: an ass is a fool
set means fixed, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A fool owns some immovable property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container; the inner word sits after the first S of the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions of value owned by a person or firm are resources.

clue.text: She gets involved with men — to do this to them maybe

definitions.text: She gets involved with men — to do this to them maybe

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A woman takes up with men in order to ensnare them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved' shuffles SHE and MEN together, and the whole clue describes a woman entangling men.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a net, or entangle, is what the woman may do to the men.

clue.text: A bloomer for which the strike-breaker promises to pay?

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker writes promissory notes for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with blue or lilac flower heads, a flower of meadows, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Kind of sandpiper that gives the debt collector nothing back

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of a debt

indicators.note: back means the word for nothing is written in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A bird gives the debt collector nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal; 'dun' is an old word for a debt collector and also the verb to demand payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading bird of shores with a red-brown back is a species in the sandpiper family.

clue.text: The girl who's been cavorting with Eric?

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Who is the girl that has been frolicking with Eric?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' mixes BEEN and ERIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, borne by a queen of ancient Egypt, is a girl's name.

clue.text: If his star players won't the football manager may have to

definitions.text: If his star players won't the football manager may have to

parts.words: If his star players won't the football manager may have to
parts.note: players who will not sign new contracts again leave the manager to quit his own job, one word in two senses

explanation.surface: A football manager faces losing his job if top players refuse new contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters mean 'sign again' (with a hyphen) for the players and 'quit' for the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Players refusing to sign again, the manager may have to step down from his post.

clue.text: Angry demonstrations in favour of international cricket matches

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Test matches are international cricket matches

explanation.surface: Fans hold furious rallies supporting Test cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: TESTS are Test matches, the long form of international cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Marches and rallies voicing objection are public outcries of this kind.
